title: Add multiplayer to your game with 1 prompt
author: Altruistic_Series258
selftext:
Hey! After having built, the hardest part is usually having a multiplayer added because you have to have your own server, thinking about sockets, rooms, etc... 

With Antics, I allow you to transform your solo player game with just 1 prompt  Give 1 prompt to claude code / codex , and it will use the MCP to change your game in a multiplayer game.



You can try it right away, no signup (unless you want the game to live longer than 24 hours) .  

Looking to game vibecoder to try it out and get feedbacks! 

Here some example:   
\- [https://antics.gg/r/A2MW8V](https://antics.gg/r/A2MW8V)  
\- [https://antics.gg/r/SX3YJU](https://antics.gg/r/SX3YJU)   
\- [https://antics.gg/r/PBYBZR](https://antics.gg/r/PBYBZR)

  
Here the prompt : 

    Add antics multiplayer to my game with antics mcp.
    
    Setup — add the antics MCP server: `claude mcp add antics -- npx -y antics-mcp`, then deploy with its deploy_game tool.
    
    Quality check before deploying: if the game uses a full-screen <canvas>, give it explicit CSS width/height (e.g. width:100%; height:100%) — `position:fixed; inset:0` alone does not stretch a canvas, and a devicePixelRatio-scaled bitmap will break mouse/camera math on hi-DPI screens.
    
    Integrate rooms + state sync (and a leaderboard if the game has scores), deploy it (a single HTML file or a multi-file project both work), and give me the playable link to share with friends.

comments.author: Yaffari
comments.body: Opslus 4.8 actually did multiplayer for me in 1 prompt.
